text:
The Flames are 7-9-1 and our numbers give them a 10% shot at the playoffs. That is the cold summary. The warmer one is that the last 10 games have gone 6-3-1, so the hole came early and the team has been climbing out of it since.

The underlying problem hasn't moved, though. Calgary has taken 45.35% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) and allowed 60 goals, 3.53 a game. The power play has produced 0.39 expected goals a game, a thin return for a team that needs goals.

Matvei Gridin is the bright spot: eight points in his last 10 on 6.4 expected, playing on the most used line with Ryan Strome and Martin Pospisil. That line has taken 43% of the expected goals, though, so the production is outrunning the territory. Kevin Bahl and Simon Nemec are the steadiest pair at about even; Jake Middleton and Zach Whitecloud have been outchanced badly, 38%.

What to watch: whether the run keeps going with chances this lopsided. Our guess is that a better power play is the only way it does.
headline: Calgary's record hides a better month
